chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Wilbur DeParis at the Pearl Theater
summary: After Bobby Lee's band broke up he joined Wilbur DeParis, who was tight with money and charged them for every meal.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And was Wilbur DeParis in that band?
No Wilbur DeParis was there, he had his own band, at that time.
In Philadelphia. He was in Atlantic City, because I didn't meet Wilbur until after I left Bobby Lee. Then I met Wilbur DeParis. In Philadelphia.
How long did you stay in Philadelphia?
Well, I stayed in Philadelphia -- must've been well I went to Atlantic City, I mean to Sea Girt with Bobby Lee. I stayed there the summer --
-- and I came back and then I joined Wilbur DeParis at the Pearl Theater. That was just about almost in -- I got into the summer.

Because Bobby Lee's band broke up after the Sea Girt Inn. And we came back and so Wilbur was there and I worked with Wilbur DeParis. At the Pearl Theater. And we played different dances around Philadelphia.
And so that wasn't very far from New York, did you -- get to New York?
Not far from New York, well not at that time. After -- the problem with Wilbur we had --

Well, Wilbur was very tight with money, at that time, you know, he was very strict and he had a rooming house in Philadelphia and he kept us -- kept us there. We lived with him and he fed us and he would keep little books and he had a regular file on everybody there and if you -- whatever you ate, he'd write it down, you know. If you had an extra biscuit, he'd write it down on the paper, so that at the end of the week at the Pearl Theater, you owed him almost everything that you made. And he was paid.
Now who else was in the -- in the Wilbur DeParis band?

Well there were Bill Dillard on trumpet, and Sidney DeParis. Jerry Blake -- I don't know who else was in that band. I can't -- I don't remember who else was in -- saxophone players -- I don't. He's always had a yen for hiring
musicians that weren't popular. He liked that he could handle them better like that.
So, I don't remember exactly who else was in that band.
